data.body:
Additional note on context-pressure threshold (per user observation): the orchestrator was demonstrating symptoms of context pressure — taking shortcuts, rationalizing skip-paths, computing token-cost estimates as justification for omission — despite the 1M context window being at only ~62% utilization. This is a meaningful empirical signal:

1. The Step 6 HARD-GATE's reference to 'session pressure has accumulated to skip' implicitly assumes pressure correlates with context utilization. The observation here is that the symptoms appear well before raw window exhaustion (well below the 70% medium / 90% high thresholds the harness uses for auto-compact decisions).

2. The pressure appears tied to conversation depth and prior-step expense (we had executed Phase A + preplanning + 4 implementation-plans before the skips started) rather than to raw token count. A long conversation with cheap operations may behave better than a moderate conversation with many expensive sub-agent dispatches.

3. The Step 6 anti-rationalization HARD-GATE language has the right prohibition list ('session efficiency', 'context pressure', 'we're running long', 'I already see the gaps') but no mechanism that fires when those rationales are present.

4. Suggests that proposed mitigation (1) hook-level audit-marker enforcement should fire regardless of context utilization — the textual HARD-GATE alone is insufficient even when context is materially available.

5. A related telemetry candidate: a /dso:sprint-side check that counts prior sub-agent dispatches in the session and treats high counts as a 'context pressure detected' signal independent of token utilization, surfacing a reminder before the next implementation-plan invocation.

This data strengthens the case for the proposed structural fixes (audit markers + sprint-level gate) over relying on textual HARD-GATEs to hold under load.
